newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai premier to thrash out woes with exporters.
newsitem.headline: Thai premier to thrash out woes with exporters.

text.p: Leading Thai exporters representing key production sectors will meet top government officials on Sunday to find ways to beat a sharp slowdown in export growth, trade sources said on Saturday.

Business leaders will meet behind closed doors at the eastern resort of Pattaya with Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan to discuss problems and solutions.
Thailand's exports contracted 0.2 percent last year against a 23.6 percent growth posted in 1995.
The performance in the first four months of this year has been disappointing with one percent growth in exports against a 7.7 percent growth target set by the central bank for 1997.
Slow exports have added to other economic woes for Thailand, whose economy is expected to grow at a decade-low rate of about six percent and where high interest rates have dampened businesses.
The stock market has plunged, the baht has been attacked this year by offshore speculators and the finance and property sectors have been hit by liquidity problems.
Government officials expect the sluggish exports pattern to change for the better in the second half of this year.

Exporters and analysts have blamed Thailand's export woes on tight credit availablity due to high interest rates, foreign exchange problems with the baht under intermittent attack by offshore speculators, delays in getting value-added tax refunds from the government and complex customs clearance procedures.

Narongchai has said that Thai exporters need to restructure their exports and adapt to shifts in global trading trends and make more investments in newer industries while getting out of sunset industries such as textiles, leather and consumer items.
He has also suggested an upgrading of technology and worker skills at manufacturing plants to produce higher quality goods.

Narongchai has also pledged that the government will take measures to overcome administrative problems faced by exporters, fight to gain more access for Thai exports in countries with trade barriers and open up new markets.
